chunks: Ibn Ribāṭ narrated to me, from Ibn Muskān, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
A man came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said: O Messenger of Allah, inform me about Islam—its root, its branch, its summit, and its highest point.
He said: Its root is salat (prayer), its branch is zakat (alms-tax), and its summit and highest point is jihad in the way of Allah, Exalted is He.

He said: O Messenger of Allah, inform me about the gates of goodness. He said: Sawm (fasting) is a shield, charity removes sin, and a man's standing in the depth of the night, privately conversing with his Lord.
Then he said: “Their sides forsake their beds; they call upon their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend out of what We have provided them.”

key_terms.الزَّكَاةُ: zakat (alms-tax), presented as a principal branch of Islam
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), presented as the root and foundation
key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: Islam as the religion whose essential structure is being described
key_terms.الْجِهَادُ: jihad, described here as the summit and highest point in the way of Allah
key_terms.جَوْفِ اللَّيْلِ: the depth of the night, the time of intimate worship and devotion
key_terms.يُنْفِقُونَ: they spend, referring to giving from what Allah has provided

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the foundation of Islam and the gates of goodness?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a concise description of Islam’s structure: salat (prayer) as its foundation, zakat (alms-tax) as its branch, and jihad in the way of Allah as its loftiest height. It then identifies key gates of goodness—sawm (fasting), charity, and night worship—ending with a Quranic verse praising those who rise at night in devotion and spend from their provision.
